money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency is the Danish Krone (DKK). If you travel between Denmark and any non-EU country, you must declare cash of over 10,000 euros (or equivalent). This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. If you don't declare or give the wrong information on entry or exit, you'll need to pay a fine. You don't need to declare cash if you're travelling to or from another EU country. ATMs are common, and credit cards are accepted in most places. Check if your credit card has 'chip and PIN' technology. Many hotels, restaurants and shops need this.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug possession, use or trafficking, even small amounts, include heavy fines and prison sentences.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: It's illegal to wear clothing which covers the face while in a public place. You'll be fined if you don't comply, and the fine increases for repeat offenders. The law applies to both residents and visitors. Penalties for vandalism, such as graffiti, may include fines, jail and/or deportation. Contact the Danish Civil Aviation and Railway Authority for more information and guidance on registration. Holders of Australian superannuation accounts should seek advice on taxation before moving to Denmark.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: For specific information on bringing medication into Denmark, refer to the Danish Medicines Agency.
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: To drive, you'll need both: a valid Australian driver's licence (digital licences may not be accepted) an International Driving Permit (IDP). You must get your IDP before leaving Australia.
laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: Trafikstyrelsen says flying in geographic drone zones (flight-safety-critical, security-critical and Natura 2000 nature areas) needs an application to it first. Some Natura 2000 zones apply only in certain seasons, such as breeding time.

Anyone entering or leaving the European Union with cash worth EUR 10,000 or more (about A$15,900 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293) must declare it to customs. Cash here means banknotes and coins, bearer cheques and similar instruments, gold and other commodities used as stores of value, and prepaid cards. Each member state sets its own penalty for not declaring; the EU regulation says penalties must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.
laws.heading: Cash declaration (EU Regulation 2018/1672)

laws.rule: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU duty-free allowance is 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus one of: 1 litre of spirits over 22% alcohol, or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine. The EU page tells travellers to check the destination country's customs for the latest limits.
laws.heading: Duty-free alcohol from outside the EU

laws.rule: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU allowance is 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of tobacco. The EU page says a lower limit (40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g of tobacco) applies to land and sea travellers in some EU countries; check this country's customs. You can mix product types but the total must stay within the limit.
laws.heading: Duty-free tobacco from outside the EU

laws.rule: Travelling into the EU from a non-EU country, you are not allowed to bring any meat or dairy products. Limited amounts of fruit and vegetables, eggs, egg products, honey and some fish are allowed. Exceptions: up to 10 kg per person from the Faroe Islands or Greenland, and up to 2 kg of powdered infant milk, infant food or special medical foods (unopened, shelf-stable, proprietary brand), or health-related pet food for an accompanying pet. Undeclared products are confiscated and destroyed, and a fine or prosecution is possible.
laws.heading: Meat and dairy from outside the EU

laws.rule: Under Article 75 of the Schengen Convention, a traveller carrying narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances for their own medical treatment must be able to produce, at a check, a certificate issued or authenticated by a competent authority of their state of residence. The certificate form covers the substance, quantity and length of the journey. How a resident of Australia obtains one is not checked in this entry; ask this country's embassy or health authority before travel.
laws.heading: Schengen certificate for narcotic or psychotropic medicines (Article 75)

laws.rule: Road Traffic Act (færdselsloven) section 53(1): driving or trying to drive a motor vehicle with more than 0.50 per mille alcohol in the blood, or more than 0.25 mg per litre in the breath, is an offence. Section 53(2): for an ordinary car (category B), the limits drop to 0.20 per mille blood or 0.10 mg per litre breath in the first 3 years after first gaining the right to drive that category, or where the driving also breaks section 56(1). Section 53(3): driving after drinking so that you cannot drive safely is also an offence.

Road Traffic Act (færdselsloven) section 54: a motor vehicle may not be driven by anyone whose blood contains a mind-altering substance classed as dangerous for road safety and not taken under a lawful prescription. For THC (the active part of cannabis) the national limit is more than 0.001 mg per kilogram of blood when it was not taken under a lawful prescription.

Knives and Blades Act (lov om knive og blankvåben m.v.) section 1: knives and blade weapons may not be carried or held in publicly accessible places, education sites or youth clubs, unless it is for work, hunting, angling or sport, or a similar recognised purpose. Section 2: some blades (over 12 cm, butterfly knives, flick knives, throwing stars and similar) need police permission to acquire, hold or carry, with exceptions in section 2(2) for work, household use, hunting, angling or sport.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Denmark is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
Greenland and the Faroe Islands aren't in Schengen or the EU.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: EU baseline (EASA): register once as an operator in the state of residence or establishment, recognised across EASA states; Specific-category work in another state needs cross-border acceptance by that state's authority. National register, zone map and visitor rules checked 6 Nov 2026 (see items); footage routes not yet checked.

items.text: Not yet checked: whether the national aviation authority publishes a list of authorised operators.

EU rules (Regulations 2019/947 and 2019/945): operators register in the EASA state where they reside or are established; Specific-category operations need an operational authorisation or a standard-scenario declaration.

An operator registered in another EASA state may fly here; for Specific-category work it first gets the authorisation or STS declaration at home, then the destination authority must confirm the cross-border operation before flying. Rules for operators from outside EASA states: not yet checked.
Not yet checked: national tourism board or film commission media libraries.

Drones over 250 g, or any carrying a sensor, need a registered operator. Trafikstyrelsen guidance and droneregler.dk differ on which site takes the registration, so the registration URL is not recorded.

Trafikstyrelsen (the transport authority) publishes the official drone zone map on droneregler.dk, taken over from Naviair in 2023. Flying in the geographic drone zones (flight-safety-critical, security-critical and Natura 2000 areas) needs an application to Trafikstyrelsen. Natura 2000 zones are shown in green; some apply only in certain seasons such as breeding time. Military areas need permission from the Defence Command, not Trafikstyrelsen.

VisitDenmark's media library page lists photos and videos for press and promotional use, and links to regional media centres (Copenhagen, Aarhus, Odense, Aalborg, Bornholm and others). Material is only for marketing and promoting Denmark as a travel destination; each regional library has its own terms. Registration and aerial footage were not stated.
